summary: In the Lishkas HaGazis the Kohanim said a bracha, the Aseres HaDibros and Shema, and more brachos. On Shabbos the group that was finishing its week added one more bracha.
stIntro: After the priests completed laying the parts of the daily offering on the ramp, they went to the Chamber of Hewn Stone to recite Shema.

chunks.en: The memuneh said to them,
chunks.st: The appointed priest who oversaw the lotteries in the Temple said to the priests:

chunks.en: "Say one bracha,"
chunks.st: Recite a single blessing of the blessings that accompany Shema.

chunks.en: and they said the bracha.
chunks.st: And the members of the priestly watch recited a blessing, and then

chunks.en: They read the Aseres HaDibros,
chunks.st: they recited the Ten Commandments,

words.note: The Aseres HaDibros, the Ten Commandments.

chunks.en: Shema, Vehayah im shamoa,
chunks.st: Shema (see Deuteronomy 6:4–9), VeHaya im Shamoa (see Deuteronomy 11:13–21),

words.note: Vehayah im shamoa, the second part of Shema.

chunks.he: וַיֹּאמֶר. בֵּרְכוּ אֶת הָעָם שָׁלשׁ בְּרָכוֹת,
chunks.en: and Vayomer. They said three brachos with the people:
chunks.st: and VaYomer (see Numbers 15:37–41), the standard formula of Shema. Additionally, they blessed with the people three blessings.

words.note: The third part of Shema, about tzitzis.

chunks.en: Emes veyatziv,
chunks.st: These blessings were: True and Firm,
chunks.stMore: the blessing of redemption recited after Shema;

words.note: Emes veyatziv, the bracha said after Shema.

chunks.en: Avodah, and Birkas Kohanim.
chunks.st: and the blessing of the Temple service, which is also a blessing recited in the Amida prayer; and the Priestly Benediction,
chunks.stMore: recited in the form of a prayer, without the lifting of hands that usually accompanies that blessing (Tosafot).

words.note: The bracha about the service in the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.he: וּבְשַׁבָּת מוֹסִיפִין בְּרָכָה אַחַת לַמִּשְׁמָר הַיּוֹצֵא:
chunks.en: And on Shabbos they add one bracha for the mishmar that is leaving.
chunks.st: And on Shabbat, when the new priestly watch would begin its service, the priests would add one blessing recited by the outgoing priestly watch,
chunks.stMore: that love, fraternity, peace, and friendship should exist among the priests of the incoming watch.

words.note: The group of Kohanim who served for one week.

summary: Next came a lottery for burning the ketores, only for Kohanim who had never done it. Then all the Kohanim joined a lottery for bringing the parts of the korban up to the mizbe'ach.

chunks.en: He said to them,
chunks.st: said to them:

chunks.en: "New ones, for the ketores, come and join the lottery."
chunks.explain: Only Kohanim who never burned the ketores could join.
chunks.st: Let only those priests who are new to burning the incense come and participate in the lottery for the incense.

chunks.en: They held the lottery, and whoever won, won.
chunks.st: Whoever won that lottery won the privilege to burn the incense. The appointed priest said to them:

chunks.en: "New ones with old ones, come and join the lottery,
chunks.st: Those new priests, i.e., those who had never performed the service, together with those old priests, i.e., those who had already performed it, may come and participate in the lottery to determine

chunks.he: מִי מַעֲלֶה אֵבָרִים מִן הַכֶּבֶשׁ לַמִּזְבֵּחַ.
chunks.en: (to see) who brings the parts from the ramp up to the mizbe'ach."
chunks.st: who takes the limbs from the bottom half of the ramp, where they had been placed earlier, up to the altar.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov says:

chunks.en: The one who brought the parts to the ramp is the one who brings
chunks.st: The priest who takes the limbs up to the ramp is the one who takes them up

chunks.en: them up onto the mizbe'ach.
chunks.st: from the ramp and places them upon the altar.

summary: The Kohanim who did not win a job gave their holy clothes to the chazzanim (helpers). There were cubbies with labels for each kind of clothing.
stIntro: The priests who did not win a lottery were still dressed in the priestly vestments that they were required to don when entering the lottery, so that if they won they would be prepared for immediate service. The appointed priest

chunks.en: They handed them over to the chazzanim.
chunks.st: handed over these priests to the care of the attendants [laḥazanim].

chunks.en: They would take off their clothes,
chunks.st: The attendants would undress these priests and remove their garments,

chunks.en: and they did not leave on them
chunks.st: and they would leave

chunks.en: anything except the pants alone.
chunks.st: only their trousers on them.
chunks.stMore: After the priests donned their non-sacred garments, they would remove the priestly trousers and don their non-sacred trousers.

chunks.en: There were windows (cubbies) there,
chunks.st: And there were four storage compartments there
chunks.stMore: in the Temple for the storage of priestly vestments for each priestly watch,

chunks.en: with the use of each piece of clothing written on them.
chunks.st: and on each of them was written the use of the garment
chunks.stMore: stored there: Trousers, tunic, belt, and mitre.

summary: The Kohen who won the ketores took a big gold spoon. Inside it was a bowl full of ketores, with a cover and a cloth on top.

chunks.en: Whoever won the ketores
chunks.st: who won the lottery to burn the incense

chunks.en: would take the spoon.
chunks.st: would take the spoon used for carrying the incense.

chunks.he: וְהַכַּף דּוֹמֶה לְתַרְקַב גָּדוֹל שֶׁל זָהָב,
chunks.en: The spoon looked like a big gold tarkav,
chunks.st: And the spoon was similar to a large gold vessel that

chunks.en: which holds three kav,
chunks.st: held three kav,

chunks.en: and the bowl was inside it,
chunks.st: and the smaller vessel was placed inside the spoon.

chunks.en: full and heaped up with ketores.
chunks.st: The vessel was filled to overflow with incense.

chunks.en: It had a cover,
chunks.st: And it had a cover to prevent spillage of the incense,

chunks.en: and a kind of cloth was on it, on top.
chunks.st: and there was a type of cloth placed upon it from above, to preserve the fragrance of the incense.

summary: A Kohen took coals from the outer mizbe'ach for the ketores. Some coals spilled and were swept away. On Shabbos they covered them with a big vessel called a pesachter, which had other uses too.

chunks.en: Whoever won the fire pan
chunks.st: who won the right to bring the coal pan
chunks.stMore: with the coals from the outer altar to the incense altar in the Sanctuary

chunks.en: took the silver fire pan,
chunks.st: took the silver coal pan,

chunks.en: and went up to the top of the mizbe'ach,
chunks.st: ascended to the top of the outer altar,

chunks.he: וּפִנָּה אֶת הַגֶּחָלִים הֵילָךְ וְהֵילָךְ וְחָתָה.
chunks.en: and pushed the coals to this side and that side, and scooped.
chunks.st: and cleared the extinguished coals from the perimeter of the flame to here and to there. Then he shoveled
chunks.stMore: four kav from the consumed inner coals, which were burned in the depths of the flame, into the coal pan.

chunks.en: He went down and poured them into the gold one.
chunks.st: He descended from the altar and emptied the coals into the coal pan made of gold.

chunks.en: About a kav of coals spilled out of it,
chunks.st: Approximately one kav of coals from it was spilled and scattered
chunks.stMore: on the courtyard floor, as the capacity of the gold pan was only three kav.

chunks.en: and he would sweep them into the water channel.
chunks.st: And a priest would sweep the scattered coals into the Temple courtyard drain
chunks.stMore: that passed through the courtyard to drain the waste outside the Temple.

words.note: A water channel that ran through the azarah.

chunks.en: And on Shabbos he would turn a pesachter over them.
chunks.st: And on Shabbat, when it is prohibited to extinguish fire, the priest would not sweep the coals into the canal; rather, he would overturn a pesakhter upon them.

chunks.he: וּפְסַכְתֵּר הָיְתָה כְלִי גָדוֹל מַחֲזֶקֶת לֶתֶךְ,
chunks.en: A pesachter was a big vessel that holds a lesech.
chunks.st: And the pesakhter was a large vessel that held a half-kor.

words.note: Half a kor, a very big measure.

chunks.en: It had two chains:
chunks.st: And since the pesakhter was a very heavy vessel, there were two chains on it,
chunks.stMore: to facilitate its standard use, removal of ashes from the altar:

chunks.en: one that he pulls it down with,
chunks.st: One chain with which a priest would pull the vessel filled with ashes down the ramp,

chunks.en: and one that he holds it with
chunks.st: and one chain that another priest would grasp

chunks.en: from above, so that it will not roll.
chunks.st: from above, so that the vessel would not roll down the ramp and the ashes would not spill.

chunks.en: It was used for three things:
chunks.st: And the pesakhter would serve three purposes:

chunks.en: they turn it over on top of
chunks.st: The priests would overturn it upon the

chunks.en: coals, and on a sheretz on Shabbos,
chunks.st: coals that scattered in the Temple during the transfer from the silver to the gold coal pan on Shabbat, and they would overturn it upon the carcass of a creeping animal found in the Temple on Shabbat,

words.note: A small dead creature that makes things tamei.

chunks.en: and they bring down the ashes in it
chunks.st: and they would take the ashes down

chunks.en: from on top of the mizbe'ach.
chunks.st: from atop the altar in it.

summary: When the Kohanim reached the space before the Heichal, one threw down the magrefah. It made a very loud sound that called Kohanim and Levi'im to come.
stIntro: The priest with the spoonful of incense and the priest with the gold coal pan filled with coals

chunks.en: They reached the space between the Ulam and the mizbe'ach.
chunks.st: reached the place between the Entrance Hall to the Sanctuary and the outer altar, on their way to the Sanctuary.

words.note: The entrance hall in front of the Heichal.

chunks.en: One took the magrefah
chunks.st: One of them took the shovel

chunks.en: and threw it between the Ulam and the mizbe'ach.
chunks.st: and threw it between the Entrance Hall and the outer altar.

chunks.en: No person in Yerushalayim could hear the voice of
chunks.st: No person could hear the voice

chunks.en: his friend because of the sound of the magrefah.
chunks.st: of another speaking to him in Jerusalem, due to the sound generated by the shovel.

chunks.en: It was used for three things:

chunks.st: Any priest who hears its sound

chunks.st: knows that his brethren the priests are entering to prostrate themselves in the Sanctuary at that time,

chunks.st: And the head of the non-priestly watch,
